notes.text: Open and align above the orange can for a gentle tactile grasp; contents not yet identified.
No motion occurred in rejected attempts. Descend 3 cm, then close gently for tactile contact.
Lift the orange can a short distance to feel loading and verify visual retention before comparing cans.
Orange retained during test but its tactile contact shifted under load. Return it to the table and compare the blue can.
Clear the orange can vertically, then move toward the blue can with fingers open.
Align with the blue can from above and descend with an open gripper, maintaining clearance during transfer.
Descend to the blue can's upper sides and close gently, sampling tactile contact before lifting.
Lift the blue can briefly and hold to compare its tactile loading with the orange can; verify retention visually.
Blue is retained, with a small downward tactile shift on lifting. Set it back down and recheck orange under matching conditions before selecting.
Raise clear of the blue can and transfer back above orange to repeat the tactile loading comparison.
Center on orange and close at the same hand height and opening used for blue, establishing an unloaded tactile reference.
Apply the same short lift used on blue and compare the tactile displacement under the can's weight.
Weight cues remain subtle. Reduce orange's pinch slightly while holding just above the table to check tactile slip safely.
Check whether the lightly pinched orange can follows a small lift; watch for contact loss rather than relying on commanded opening.
Orange still follows with very light contact. Ease the opening slightly more over its original table position to test slip without moving laterally.
Orange released at the slightly wider opening. Move clear to blue for the same light-contact comparison.
Regrasp blue at the same height for the matched low-pinch load test.
Lift blue and ease to the opening that still retained orange; compare tactile slip and visual following.
Re-establish a secure pinch on blue and raise it to transport height. Tactile loading suggests blue is the lighter candidate, though the difference is subtle.
Blue remains visibly retained. Carry the selected lighter candidate toward the basket with clearance above the other can.
Move the retained blue can over the basket center while maintaining rim clearance.
Centered over the basket, ease the can down slightly and open the fingers to release it inside.
Hold open above the basket while the released can settles; check its final placement.
Blue is visibly inside the basket. Withdraw upward with fingers open and allow placement to stabilize.
Retreat to a clear raised position, leaving the selected can in the basket and the other can undisturbed.
Remain clear with the gripper open; blue is settled in the basket and orange remains on the table.
Maintain the clear pose while observing the selected can's stable placement.
Keep the arm clear and fingers open; the blue can remains inside the basket.
Maintain the safe withdrawn pose without disturbing the placed can.
Keep clear of the basket; the selected blue can remains visibly settled inside.
Maintain the withdrawn pose and leave the selected can undisturbed in the basket.
Keep the arm safely clear; the blue can remains inside the basket.
Maintain clearance and leave the placed blue can undisturbed while observing.
Hold the safe withdrawn pose; blue remains settled in the basket.
Keep the arm clear and leave the placed can undisturbed.
Maintain the withdrawn pose; the selected blue can remains visibly inside the basket.
Remain safely withdrawn with fingers open; the selected can is stable inside the basket.
Keep the arm clear and the placed can undisturbed while observing the stable basket placement.
